column1: # Two columns, separated by a TAB: what the flag SHOULD be, then the headline.
# IMPORTANT: these are hand-written examples in the style of real headlines,
# not headlines actually scraped from news sites. They are enough to get the
# rules roughly right and to catch obvious mistakes, but the rules cannot be
# properly trusted until this file is replaced with several hundred real
# headlines pulled from feeds you actually read. Adding those is a real task,
# not a formality: it is the difference between a flag people trust and a flag
# Should be left completely alone. Ordinary, honest reporting.
